body: AI financial advisers set a client's stock allocation largely from one stated-risk question, yet people do not answer it the same way twice: in a national US panel, 41% of households chose a different answer two years later, and in a laboratory retest a third of people moved two or more points on a 0-10 scale after six months. Seven large language models from five providers gave one-turn allocation advice for 800 real household profiles in which only the risk answer changed. The recommended stock share moved by 10 to 16 percentage points on average, and by 24 to 35 when the answer changed, against 0.6 to 4.2 points for the same prompt asked twice; in the laboratory retest the rating alone moved advice by 11 to 18 points. Without any note, the models respond to the answer about as strongly as when told that it is very reliable (less so for the two Claude models). If that instructed response is how each model maps attitude to advice, discounting the answer for its measured reliability, as classical test theory prescribes, would cut the swings by a factor of 2.4 to 3.3. The swing is largest for clients under 40. A note that the answer is noisy steadies some models, but shifts their weight to the client's age and pulls cautious clients towards a generic middle allocation: clients unwilling to take any risk are advised 22% stocks instead of 4%. Three extra money questions reduce the swing for some models, with no statistically detectable change relative to how much advice differs across people. In a scripted test, one clarifying question removes nearly all of the swing from an answer the client then corrects (33.5 points to 1.9 on average) while keeping the response to a change the client confirms. We argue that same-person retest audits should be a standard check for AI advisers, and that what to do with an unreliable answer is a question of client autonomy as well as of statistics.
summaryZh: 同一个人，不同的建议：通过重复的风险承受能力审核LLM财务建议。人工智能财务顾问主要根据一个明确的风险问题来设定客户的股票配置，但人们不会以同样的方式回答两次：在美国全国小组中，41%的家庭在两年后选择了不同的答案，在实验室重新测试中，三分之一的人在六个月后在0-10等级上移动了两个或更多点。来自 5 个提供商的 7 个大型语言模型为 800 个真实家庭资料提供了一轮分配建议，其中只有风险答案发生了变化。
